target_customer: Software companies (HR tech, recruiting, benefits, fintech) that need integrations with their customers' HRIS, ATS and payroll systems
problem: Each HR, recruiting and payroll system has its own API, so software vendors spend engineering time building and maintaining dozens of separate integrations.
business_model: Usage and subscription priced unified API, developer infrastructure
product_category: Unified API for HR, payroll and recruiting integrations

technical_complexity.rationale: Normalizing data models across dozens of vendor APIs, auth flows and sync logic is standard engineering with a long tail of maintenance.

defensibility.rationale: Once embedded in a customer's product, integrations are costly to replace; the integration catalog takes time to build but rivals sell the same idea.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals kept operating; Kombo reports 300+ customers by 2026 and acquired Midlane per a search snippet.

market_need_then: SaaS vendors needed many HR integrations; the YC description frames the pain of building one per recruiting system.

outcome_analysis: Kombo is active, has grown to roughly 77 people per the YC page, claims 300+ customers and raised a 25M Series A in February 2026 led by Volition Capital after a 2.5M round in 2025. The company sells infrastructure with embedded integrations, which creates switching costs, but it competes directly with Merge and Finch. Execution speed and a focused developer wedge explain the growth.
